newsitem.title: UK: Thames, water stocks hit by Ofwat attack.
newsitem.headline: Thames, water stocks hit by Ofwat attack.

text.p: Shares in Thames Water Plc and other UK water stocks dropped in pre-market trading on Wednesday after a press report that the industry regulator had attacked recent large dividend increases in the sector.

In an interview with the Financial Times, Ofwat chief Ian Byatt said recent double-digit dividend increases from the likes of Anglian Water Plc and Yorkshire Water Plc were unsustainable and politically dangerous.

The paper quoted Byatt as saying he was "very puzzled" over why such dividend increases were felt necessary and warned that big dividend increases encouraged a view that the government's planned "windfall" tax on utilities was a good idea.

By 0725 GMT, Thames was down 7p at 683, United Utilities Plc was down 2-1/2p at 692-1/2, Anglian Water dropped 5-1/2p to 669-1/2, Severn Trent Plc fell 5p to 779-1/2, Yorkshire Water Plc was down 2p at 381-1/2, Hyder Plc was down 4-1/2p at 804, Wessex Water Plc eased 3p to 681 and South West Water Plc fell 6-1/2p to 722-1/2.
Dealers said Byatt's comments had not raised undue concerns about the water companies' dividend outlook and noted he was not talking about action against high dividend increases.
"It is just a small scare, there was just an early mark-down in the shares," said one market maker.
No one at Ofwat was immediately available for comment on the interview.
